P&E Foods operates from Honolulu, Hawaii, where it was established in 1975 as a family-owned wholesale distributor. The business traces its roots to 1943, when the grandparents of the current owner launched the Jungle Wagon to supply U.S. soldiers training in Ka‘a‘awa.

The company imports primarily frozen meats and seafood from the mainland and international sources, stocking over 600 products in its local warehouse. It provides wholesale distribution, warehousing, and product sourcing for customers across the islands, with the ability to locate items not currently in inventory.

P&E Foods serves major supermarket chains and neighborhood restaurants throughout Hawaii. Its customer base spans large-scale grocery retailers and independent foodservice operators, reflecting a focus on both high-volume and small-order accounts.

The company emphasizes a customer-first approach, treating clients like ‘ohana’ (family).

name: PB2 Foods, Inc.
old_description: Freshly Roasted Peanuts are pressed to remove most of the oil. Add a little sugar and a dash of salt for flavor and the result is peanut butter with 90% less fat and nearly 70% fewer calories than traditional peanut butter.
about:
PB2 Foods, Inc. is headquartered in Tifton, Georgia. The company was launched in 2007 with a mission to help people find balance in everyday life through a line of plant-based products. While the founders are not named in public materials, the business began by developing a process that presses freshly roasted peanuts to remove most of the oil, creating a powdered peanut butter with significantly reduced fat and calories.

The company manufactures powdered nut butters, plant-based protein powders, pantry baking mixes, and a natural peanut butter spread. Its core process involves roasting U.S.-grown peanuts and pressing them to extract oil, then blending with ingredients such as sugar, salt, allulose, or palm oil depending on the product. Facility size, headcount, and production volumes are not disclosed.

PB2 products are sold directly to consumers through the company website and through major retailers nationwide and online marketplaces such as Amazon.

The company emphasizes that food can be both healthy and delicious, working closely with a network of family farmers to ensure consistent quality. Its differentiators include a clean-label approach, non-GMO ingredients, and products designed for versatile use in smoothies, baking, and spreads.

about:
PCS Electronics, LLC was founded in 2010 by Michael Klinginsmith in Columbia, Missouri.

The firm operates as an authorized dealer and service center for Generac, Kohler, Onan, and Magnum Energy, offering standby generators, portable generators, transfer switches, and power inverters. In addition to generator systems, PCS Electronics stocks a range of electronic components—including capacitors, resistors, relays, fuses, LEDs, and Arduino accessories—and provides preventative maintenance plans that follow NFPA 110 guidelines for transfer switch upkeep.

Customers are primarily homeowners seeking automatic standby power for medical needs or outage protection, as well as worksite and recreational users needing portable generation. The company also supports light commercial installations through its free in-home consultation and evaluation service.

PCS Electronics differentiates itself through factory-trained technicians—Kohler Service-Learning Academy, Generac factory training in Eagle, Wisconsin, and Onan HSB air-cooled certification—and over 12 years as an authorized warranty service center for Magnum Energy inverters.

old_description: Data Centers, Prefabricated Electrical Skids, Switchgear, and
about:
PCX Corporation was founded in 1993 and operates from its headquarters in Clayton, North Carolina, with a dedicated manufacturing facility in nearby Knightdale. From its start, PCX focused on delivering what it calls "Predictive Profitability®" through integrated system solutions engineered and prebuilt offsite at competitive prices and shortened delivery times.

The company designs and manufactures modular data centers, prefabricated electrical skids, switchgear, and switchboards. These prebuilt modular systems range from simple skids and ISO containers to custom modules, enclosures, and E‑buildings. PCX's engineering team uses AutoCAD 3D Inventor solid modeling, ETAP power‑system software, and RISA structural design tools to optimize layouts, claiming up to a 25% reduction in required electrical space versus customer originals. All projects are built to NEC and UL standards, and factory witness testing covers mechanical, electrical, cooling, power, and fire systems before shipment.

PCX serves data‑center operators (enterprise, colocation, edge, and hyperscale), commercial‑construction contractors, and the utility and renewable‑energy sectors worldwide. Its vendor‑neutral approach allows it to integrate best‑of‑breed components for new builds and facility expansions alike.

The firm's stated differentiator is its "Predictive Profitability®" promise: by moving construction offsite, it aims to accelerate schedules by up to 50%, reduce costs, and mitigate risk through fixed schedules without costly change orders.

old_description: PDI has been family owned and operated since 1994.  Our 25,000 sq ft auto parts warehouse and corporate headquarters has always been located at 6155 Forest Home Ave, Milwaukee WI.  In 1995, we became an official Federated Auto Parts Member.  At that time, we were mainly a WD warehouse serving independent Jobbers.  Since then, we have transitioned to a model that directly serves the professional independent automotive repair facility through our own company owned wholesale locations.
about:
Parts Distributing Inc. (PDI) has been a family-owned auto parts distributor in Waukesha, Wisconsin, since 1994. The company began as a 25,000-square-foot warehouse and corporate headquarters in Milwaukee, initially operating as a WD warehouse serving independent jobbers. In 1995, PDI became an official Federated Auto Parts member.

Today PDI operates four wholesale locations across southeastern Wisconsin totaling nearly 50,000 square feet, including sites in Milwaukee South, Milwaukee North, Waukesha, and Sheboygan. The company supplies brand-name replacement parts to professional independent automotive and fleet repair facilities, supported by online ordering integrations with Federated Link, Mitchell/Shop Key, NexPart, PartsTech, and RO Writer.

PDI serves repair shops throughout Fond du Lac, Kenosha, Milwaukee, Ozaukee, Racine, Sheboygan, and Waukesha counties. Its customer base consists of small independent repair businesses that rely on prompt deliveries and knowledgeable staff to minimize downtime.

The company emphasizes honest communication about product lines and service, employee empowerment, and respect for customers' time—values shaped by its own experience as a small business. PDI traces its expansion to the 1996 acquisition of Ridge Motor Parts and Engines Stores 6161, the 2008 opening of PDI-North, and the 2013 launch of PDI-Sheboygan.

name: PECA Labs
old_description: Founded by a group of Carnegie Mellon alumni including a pediatric surgeon, PECA Labs is revolutionizing cardiovascular implantable devices with a polymer platform and a novel design approach.
about:
PECA Labs is headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The company was founded by a group of Carnegie Mellon University alumni, including pediatric surgeon Dr. Arush Kalra, along with Doug Bernstein and Jamie Quinterno. The trio, all recognized on Forbes 30 Under 30 lists, established the venture to develop cardiovascular implantable devices based on a proprietary polymer platform.

The company designs and manufactures a family of polymeric cardiovascular implants. Its product line includes radiopaque vascular grafts with embedded markers for noninvasive imaging, controllably expandable grafts that allow pre-implant customization and post-implant growth, anti-thrombogenic grafts with an inherent bio-inert surface, the MASA Valve polymeric pulmonary valved conduit for pediatric reconstruction, and the STEALTH transcatheter aortic valve with fully polymeric leaflets. PECA reports thousands of implants of its radiopaque graft to date.

PECA Labs serves the cardiovascular medical device market, with a focus on pediatric and adult congenital heart surgery. Its devices are used in hospital settings and clinical trials; the MASA Valve, for example, is being evaluated in an FDA early feasibility study at five U.S. sites, with the first human implant performed at Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia in June 2023.

The company’s differentiation rests on its tunable polymer platform, which enables radiopacity without added metals, controllable expansion for growth accommodation, and a bio-inert surface that does not rely on drug coatings that can wear off. The platform also allows fully polymeric leaflets that permit slimmer delivery systems for transcatheter valves.

name: PF Meat Company
old_description: We are passionate about crafting unforgettable moments through food—from our carefully curated butcher case and signature Kitchen creations to our convenient Grab & Go and Take & Bake selections. Our deepest desire is to set the table for a memorable experience.
about:
PF Meat Company operates from its headquarters in Belton, South Carolina, with two retail butcher markets in Pendleton, South Carolina, and Toccoa, Georgia. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The business combines retail butchery with in-house manufacturing. Its USDA-inspected smokehouse produces a line of handcrafted smoked meats including snack sticks, smoked sausages, beef jerky, coil sausage, deli ham, whole hams, Canadian bacon, pulled pork barbecue, and signature smoked and naturally cured bacon. The company also roasts its own coffee in four signature blends—light, medium, dark, and decaf—and runs PF Kitchen at the Pendleton location, serving breakfast and lunch made with locally sourced ingredients. Additionally, PF Meat Company offers whole and half beef shares sourced from its own herd and a network of partner farms across the tri-state area.

The company serves walk-in customers at its two markets, as well as customers placing special orders from the butcher counter. Its products reach consumers seeking locally raised meats, house-roasted coffee, and ready-to-eat meals, all supported by relationships with more than 100 local and regional farms and family businesses.

PF Meat Company states its purpose is to connect people back to the land and the life it produces, strengthening local agriculture and creating spaces where people gather around good food. The "Farmer Approved" ethos emphasizes that every purchase sustains the farms and small businesses that make the region unique.

old_description: PMB Inc. is a privately-owned company, founded in 1998 by current Owner/President Tom Roth.
about:
PMB Inc. operates from Poplar Bluff, Missouri, where it was founded in 1998 by Tom Roth, who continues to serve as owner and president. The privately held company began as a plastic injection molding operation and has since expanded its footprint to two facilities totaling 48,000 square feet.

The company specializes in plastic injection molding, offering both high- and low-volume production, insert molding, and prototype runs. Its 17 presses range from 55 to 720 tons of clamping force, supporting over 100 molds that vary from single-cavity tools to complex 64-cavity production molds. In-house capabilities include mold design, construction, maintenance, and repair, as well as engineering services such as DFM review, cost estimating, and project management. Secondary operations cover automation, hot-plate welding, sonic welding, hot stamping, label application, and assembly.

PMB serves customers in the lawn and garden, sporting goods, agricultural, medical, and automotive sectors. The company works with a broad base of clients across these industries, providing molded components and value‑added assembly.

PMB emphasizes low‑cost, high‑quality injection molding backed by complete in‑house tooling support and a range of secondary processes that reduce the need for outside vendors.

The company manufactures outdoor furniture including Adirondack chairs, dining sets, deep seating, chaise lounges, rockers, and in-pool furniture. Finished pieces are shipped directly to consumers and commercial clients, with a white-glove delivery option that includes assembly and placement.

POLYWOOD serves residential customers through its direct-to-consumer website and showrooms, and supplies the commercial hospitality sector via a dedicated Commercial & Hospitality program. Its furniture is specified for hotels, resorts, restaurants, and public spaces.

The brand differentiates itself with a 20-year warranty, low-maintenance materials that resist splintering, rotting, cracking, and fading, and a commitment to U.S. manufacturing since its founding. about:
PSC Industries, Inc. traces its roots to 1954 when D. Covington Logan founded Packaging Service Corporation in Louisville, Kentucky. Logan, drawing on his industrial packaging background, aimed to serve small businesses that lacked in‑house packaging engineers. The company quickly expanded beyond that niche, and by 1962 had added a warehouse and manufacturing facility to support faster delivery. In 1987, PMC Global, Inc. acquired PSC, integrating it into a global footprint that now comprises 22 facilities across the United States, Mexico, and China.

Today PSC operates as a contract fabricator of non‑metallic materials, converting foam, rubber, fiberglass, silicone, adhesives, tapes, films, and non‑wovens into custom components. Its core processes include die cutting (rotary, laser, water‑jet, flat‑bed, and 3D contour), molding, laminating, rapid prototyping, and custom packaging, supported by engineering services for design and material selection. The company also runs testing programs for temperature, acoustics, compression, and weight properties.

PSC serves a broad industrial base, with documented customers in HVAC, appliance, automotive, office interior, aerospace, electronics, medical, and metal‑building sectors. Its capabilities pages cite automotive, appliance, HVAC, and aerospace as primary markets for die cutting, water‑jet cutting, and molding work.

The founder’s original vision — providing packaging expertise to companies without dedicated engineers — remains a differentiator, reinforced by a claim to the market’s most extensive die‑cutting equipment lineup and a quality system anchored by ISO 9001 certifications at multiple sites.

about:
Plastic Technologies, Inc. (PTI) was founded in 1985 by Thomas E. Brady, PhD, in Toledo, Ohio. Brady, who previously led PET bottle technology development at Owens-Illinois from 1971 to 1984, established the company after Coca-Cola engaged him to convert its iconic glass bottle to plastic. The firm is now headquartered in Holland, Ohio.

PTI provides integrated packaging innovation and material science services, including testing and analytical services, product design and development, finite element analysis and simulation, and a production lab. The company operates certified packaging performance testing laboratories in the United States and Luxembourg, accredited by APR, EPBP, and RecyClass. Its production capabilities range from single units to multi-million-unit runs, covering carbonated soft drink, hot-fill and aseptic, flexible, and thermoform packaging. PTI also offers training programs in PET technology, injection molding, and blow molding.

The company serves food and beverage, personal care, household products, pharmaceutical and medical, and chemical and industrial markets. Its client roster includes global brands such as Dr Pepper Snapple Group, Fair Oaks Farms (fairlife), and SC Johnson, as well as entrepreneurial startups. PTI maintains offices in the United States, Switzerland, and India.

PTI positions itself as a lab-to-market partner that reduces iteration cycles, cost, and waste while accelerating speed to market. The firm emphasizes root-cause problem solving, bridging design and functionality, and protecting customer intellectual property. Its founding mission stemmed from the need for independent PET expertise after Brady's work with Coca-Cola.

The privately held company was founded in 1984 as Proto-Tech Industries, producing functional prototype molds and injection-molded samples before adopting its current name in 1987 to reflect a turnkey, mind-to-manufacturing model.

Stocked bus bar assemblies can ship the same day, and all switchgear carries UL listing with integrated metering, communications, and monitoring.

The company serves commercial construction, industrial and institutional facilities, photovoltaic and EV infrastructure, data centers, healthcare, and emerging AI‑focused projects.

Pacific Electric differentiates itself through a culture built on integrity, safety, and customer focus. Its retrofit approach extends equipment life and reduces downtime, while same‑day shipping on standard bus bars accelerates project schedules. The firm emphasizes sustainable practices and collaborative problem‑solving to meet evolving electrification demands.

about:
Packet Digital is based in Fargo, North Dakota. Founded in 2003, the company began as a developer of power-saving computer chips before expanding into wireless tracking systems for agriculture and logistics. The founders are not named in the source material.

Today the company designs, manufactures, assembles, and tests smart batteries and power systems for unmanned aerial systems (UAS). Operations span a 25,000-square-foot battery pack manufacturing and assembly facility equipped with a surface-mount technology line, laser welders, and thermal chambers, plus an 80,000-square-foot battery cell manufacturing campus under the Badland Batteries subsidiary that broke ground in 2024. The firm has produced runs such as 10,000 printed circuit boards for an agricultural technology customer.

Customers include the U.S. Marines, U.S. Navy, Air Force Research Laboratory, and commercial UAS platforms worldwide. The company also serves the space sector with power components for CubeSats and the agriculture technology sector through partners like 701x, which uses GPS-enabled smart ear tags for cattle management.

Packet Digital emphasizes U.S.-based production, claiming the first battery factory in North Dakota and the first in the United States to manufacture cells specifically for drones and unmanned systems. Its smart batteries integrate real-time monitoring of state of charge, cell temperature, and fault reporting to extend flight time and improve safety. The company holds CMMC Level 2 certification for defense work.

about:
Patience Metal Fab operates from Brooklyn Center, Minnesota, and was founded in 2012. The shop began as a team of automotive enthusiasts and fabrication specialists focused on turning customer concepts into finished vehicles, earning a reputation across the Midwest as the “Last Stop Fab Shop” for completing projects other shops could not.

The company provides a range of fabrication services including MIG and TIG welding of aluminum, steel, and stainless steel; lathe and mill machining; tube bending; sheet-metal forming with brakes, bead rollers, slip rolls, and an English wheel; and composite and lightweight-alloy work. In-house capabilities extend to 3D scanning, CFD simulation, certified roll-cage construction, custom chassis fabrication, exhaust systems, forced-induction plumbing, engine swaps, and aero design. The shop reports more than 20,000 hours of cage and chassis fabrication experience.

Patience Metal Fab serves the motorsports and street-rod segments, working with individual builders, race teams, and restoration projects. Past projects include a NASA AIX/SU Mustang, a Camaro ZL1 LE built for Nick Plocienik, a Volkswagen MK2 VR6 nicknamed “Waskly,” and a 1950s Ford F1 restomod known as “Gramps.”

The business was started to address a gap in the market for a fabrication shop that could handle unique, difficult builds and see them through to completion, a mission reflected in its “Last Stop Fab Shop” moniker and its emphasis on 3D scanning and simulation to validate designs before cutting metal.

All products are produced in the United States. The software automates drug information capture, label template selection, beyond-use date calculation, and packaging initiation, while the feeders operate without custom canisters for unattended or high-speed tabletop packaging.

Pearson Medical Technologies serves pharmacies, hospitals, long-term care facilities, and retail pharmacies across the United States, with installations reported in Florida, Pennsylvania, Georgia, North Carolina, Ohio, New York, and Illinois, as well as internationally. Its solutions target medication packaging, dispensing accuracy, and regulatory compliance such as the Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA).

The company differentiates itself by offering two non-canister automated feeder options, a feature it claims is unique in the market. Its 1-Click Print® Technology eliminates manual keyboarding for most packaging runs, and the company reports a 99.9% dispensing accuracy rate across facilities. Patient safety and DSCSA compliance are cited as core drivers behind its product development.

about:
Peliton Plastics was founded in 1996 by Robert McKinnon in Valdosta, Georgia. The company remains family-owned and operates from a 35,000-square-foot facility in South Georgia, where it has built a full-service plastic injection molding and contract manufacturing operation over nearly three decades.

The shop runs 55- to 650-ton molding machines capable of shot sizes from 0.001 to 5 pounds, processing a wide range of thermoplastics and engineered resins. Beyond molding, Peliton provides insert molding, overmolding, in-house mold making and repair (including EDM and mold texturing), CNC milling, turning, and grinding, as well as pad and screen printing on plastics, vinyl, metal, and glass. Assembly services include ultrasonic welding, kitting, packaging, and shipping, while a 3D printing capability supports prototyping and low-volume runs.

Customers span medical devices, agriculture, automotive, kitchen products, toys, pest control, industrial components, electronic enclosures, promotional products, home and office goods, and tools. The company also works directly with inventors, offering NDA-protected development from concept to market-ready product.

Peliton emphasizes domestic production as a differentiator: all tooling, molding, finishing, and printing occur under one roof, eliminating overseas shipping delays and protecting intellectual property. The team specializes in reshoring projects, offering fast partial-order shipments and direct access to the production floor for real-time communication.

The company differentiates itself through its in-house design and tooling partnerships, open material capabilities, and a commitment to eco-friendly practices such as recycled-content packaging. It positions its service as a balance of quality and budget, aiming to reduce material waste and deliver timely shipments.

name: PharoPLAST Injection Molding
old_description: PharoPlast delivers engineering-led injection molding for companies that can’t afford rework.
about:
PharoPLAST Injection Molding operates from Cleveland, Ohio, where it was founded in 1972 as Innovations in Plastic with a single injection molding machine in a small rented space. The company transitioned to its current name in 2022 when Christopher Miedza, a longtime tooling and design partner, assumed ownership. Today it remains a family-owned business led by Christopher and his son Simon Miedza, who directs sales and regional growth across the Midwest.

The shop provides engineering-led thermoplastic injection molding backed by in-house product design, DFM/DFA guidance, tooling sourcing, refurbishment, and transfer services. It also offers reshoring support, additive prototyping, and secondary operations such as assembly, welding, decoration, and packaging. PharoPLAST emphasizes flexible volume production with no minimum order quantity and advertises 24-hour lead times once tooling is on site.

Primary customers are OEMs and manufacturers in industrial, electrical, and equipment markets. Long-standing accounts include Parker Hannifin, Eaton, and Steris. The company focuses on the Midwest corridor — Ohio, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Kentucky, West Virginia — and works with businesses of all sizes, maintaining a dedicated small-project division for runs as low as 50 parts.

PharoPLAST was built on the premise that most molding problems originate before a part reaches the press. By integrating engineering early — catching warpage, sink, and assembly conflicts before steel is cut — the company aims to eliminate rework, compress launch timelines, and give customers transparent tooling ownership and direct access to decision-makers.

about:
Phoenix Design Concepts Inc. operates from Indianapolis, Indiana, where it was founded in 2010 as an expansion of a predecessor company that had specialized in performance wear for over two decades. The business is owned by Diana Baisa, who brought more than 40 years of fashion-industry experience, including training at a European master tailoring school, and earlier ran the custom dress and suit operation Coffield & Co. serving show choirs nationwide.

The company provides cut-and-sew manufacturing for custom garments, including show choir dresses, suits, performance wear, and face masks. Its OSHA-compliant facility houses over 58 commercial manual and computerized sewing machines, multiple vacuum-powered cutting tables, and modern design and production software, all maintained by an in-house mechanic. Production is organized in three volume tiers: 10–50 pieces per style for small runs, 51–1,000 pieces for mid-level factory runs, and 1,001–5,000 pieces for larger factory runs.

Customers include schools and show choir programs that have used the Coffield Collection brand, as well as brands and businesses nationwide seeking custom sewn goods. The company also partners with local schools to provide paid entry-level positions for students interested in the fashion and cut-and-sew industry.

Phoenix Design Concepts emphasizes domestic production—all design, cutting, and sewing are performed in central Indiana—and a workforce development mission that includes training sewing engineers through a two-week onboarding program. The company cites competitive pricing, rigorous quality control at each assembly step, and a 24-hour customer service response commitment as key differentiators.

old_description: Since 1993, we have been partnering with our customers to provide them with turnkey manufacturing solutions through production machining and plastic injection molding services. Our goal has always been to make their lives easier, saving them both time and money!
about:
Plas-Tech Tooling Inc. was founded in 1993 by Dean and Marcia Sonquist in Garner, Iowa. The business began in the couple’s garage, initially focused on injection mold building and repair for local manufacturers. By 1996 the operation had outgrown that space and moved to its current location in Garner, where it has expanded into a full-service machining and molding facility.

Today the company operates both a CNC machine shop and an injection molding department under one roof. Its machining lineup includes multiple Hurco vertical mills (VM10, VM30, VMX42, VMX50), Haas and Hurco lathes with live tooling and bar feeders, and a Puma 2600SYB II with opposing spindle. For molding, it runs a 300-ton JSW 280 ADS electric press and a 180-ton Sumitomo SH160 hydraulic press. Value‑added services include assembly, kitting, welding, inventory management, CAD drafting (SolidWorks, Mastercam), reverse engineering with a portable Hexagon CMM, and design‑for‑manufacturability feedback.

The shop serves a range of industries, with a noted focus on electronic‑industry fixturing using specialty plastics. It also supports startups and established OEMs that need rapid prototypes, emergency machining (including after‑hours response), or high‑volume “lights‑out” molding. Past work includes machining a critical part from solid bar stock when a casting supplier failed, delivering parts within weeks, and running high‑volume molding campaigns on electric presses.

Plas-Tech emphasizes the flexibility of a small company combined with the reliability and technology of a larger one. Its differentiators include in‑house tool design and build, no‑minimum‑quantity rapid machining, emergency machining with 24‑hour contact, and an ISO 9001:2015‑certified quality system that targets 100 % on‑time delivery and 100 % right‑first‑time components.

name: Plastic Recycling Of Iowa Falls Inc
old_description: Manufacturing quality plastic products while protecting the environment
about:
Plastic Recycling of Iowa Falls, Inc. operates from Iowa Falls, Iowa. The business traces its roots to 1986 when Hammer's Plastic Recycling began processing mixed plastic and manufacturing products from commingled material. In 1984, Hammer's had formed Plastic Recycling, Inc. to design and build a production facility for recycling mixed-plastic waste. The company won the Iowa Governor's Award in 1988. New management took over in 1997, and the name changed to Plastic Recycling of Iowa Falls in 1999.

The company manufactures a range of recycled-plastic products including park benches, picnic tables, planters, trash receptacles, traffic safety items such as car stops and speed bumps, landscape timbers, posts, dimensional lumber, and custom-molded parts. Production runs on automated lines for large-profile items, supported by patented equipment that enables custom molding with low-cost mold design. The firm's unique molds and processes are protected by multiple U.S. and international patents.

Customers include the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, the National Park system, state and city governments, and industrial manufacturers. Washington State Parks has installed over 2,000 picnic tables; Marshall Engines uses recycled-plastic skids for shipping remanufactured engines; the Smithsonian Institution relied on the lumber for supporting a historic bell; and the City of Norwalk Parks and Recreation purchased hex tables for its aquatic center.

The company was founded to address the landfill crisis by turning plastic waste into a community resource. It emphasizes a minimum 96% recycled content (by weight) with additives limited to 4%, UV stabilizers molded in, and products that require no painting, staining, or sealing and resist warping, splintering, and rot.

about:
Plastimold Products operates from a 33,000-square-foot facility in Delray Beach, Florida. The company was founded in 1999 when Joe Parisi Sr., an optical-industry veteran, purchased a small injection molding shop in Fort Lauderdale. After moves to Boca Raton (2003) and Delray Beach (2007), the business remains family-owned and is now led by second-generation owners Joe and Anthony Parisi.

The shop provides custom plastic injection molding and precision CNC machining under one roof. Its 32 all-electric presses range from 45 to 390 tons with shot sizes up to 52 ounces, supporting scientific molding, overmolding, insert molding, and in-house toolmaking. CNC capabilities include 5-axis and mill/turn machining on Makino, Okuma, Mazak, and Haas machines for aerospace alloys, medical components, and mold tooling. The company handles prototype through full-scale production, with a focus on mid-to-high volumes and short runs of 1,000–10,000 parts. Assembly services such as adhesive bonding, ultrasonic welding, and fulfillment round out the offering.

Plastimold serves OEMs in aerospace, medical, defense, firearms, consumer goods, and industrial markets. Programs often involve tight-tolerance components in high-temperature polymers (PEEK, Ultem, Delrin) and structural resins, with full traceability required by AS9100, ISO 13485, and ITAR regulations.

The company emphasizes single-source responsibility—molding, machining, tooling, and inspection stay in the same plant to shorten communication loops and maintain consistent run-to-run quality. Family ownership keeps engineering leadership close to the floor, and a gated DFM-to-delivery process aims to deliver audit-ready traceability on every shipment.

Powerwise Systems is based in Bucksport, Maine, and was founded in 2010. The company emerged from a team that previously worked at RainWise, Inc., a 47-year-old weather station manufacturer. Its platform provides whole-house energy monitoring, BTU metering for thermal systems, and solar production tracking. Powerwise also performs MET station installation and commissioning, civil work, and ongoing operations and maintenance for large-scale photovoltaic installations.

The systems serve utility-scale solar farms, commercial rooftop arrays, and multi-tenant properties seeking granular energy cost allocation. The company’s vendor relationships span EKO Instruments, Campbell Scientific, Hukseflux, Kipp & Zonen, RainWise, RM Young, and Atonometrics.

Powerwise differentiates itself through deep domain expertise: its lead engineer authored the first edition of the SunSpec standard for weather stations, and the team brings over 40 years of weather station experience. The firm tailors MET systems to project specifications and budgets, offering a single source for hardware, installation, and long-term service.

about:
Pratt (Bell Packaging), Inc., operating as Pratt Industries, is headquartered in Wyoming, Michigan. Founded in 1985, the company is privately held and has grown into the fifth-largest corrugated packaging company in the United States and the world's largest privately held producer of 100% recycled containerboard.

The company operates a vertically integrated supply chain that spans 19 recycling facilities, six paper mills, 21 corrugating plants, 25 converting plants, 17 retail display facilities, and 46 transportation facilities. Its hub-and-spoke network collects recyclable materials while delivering finished boxes, feeding recovered fiber into its mills to produce 100% recycled paper for corrugated sheets, packaging, and displays. A customer team of over 300 supports design, logistics, and supply-chain management.

Pratt serves a range of industries with a noted focus on the Southeast agriculture market, providing custom corrugated boxes, palletized truckloads, and retail displays. Its logistics division manages dedicated fleets, brokerage, and shipping agency services for local, regional, and national distribution.

The company's differentiation rests on its "green mission" — using recycling as a tool against climate change — and its independence as a privately held business that prioritizes people, customers, and the planet. In 2022, executive chairman Anthony Pratt pledged a $5 billion investment in U.S. recycling and clean energy infrastructure, aiming to create 5,000 manufacturing jobs by 2032.

old_description: Innovation is far more than just a good idea or a successful product. At Precision Fabrics, innovation is our passion. It fuels our work and is the keystone to our success.
about:
Precision Fabrics Group is headquartered in Greensboro, North Carolina, with manufacturing plants in North Carolina and Virginia. The company was created in 1988 when Lanty L. Smith led a leveraged buyout of the Precision Fabrics Division from Burlington Industries, and it remains a privately held business today. Smith, a former president of Burlington, founded the company to acquire the existing textile operations and steer them toward engineered materials.

The company produces highly technical woven and nonwoven engineered materials. Its Vinton, Virginia plant specializes in weaving continuous-filament fabrics, while the Greensboro, North Carolina facility focuses on a broad range of nonwoven products. Core processes include fine-filament weaving, finishing, and the application of chemistries and laminations to nonwoven substrates. Precision Fabrics employs approximately 600 associates and offers a wide spectrum of technical properties such as acoustic absorption, flame resistance, antimicrobial protection, electromagnetic interference shielding, and fluid repellency.

Precision Fabrics serves high-performance industries including aerospace, military, medical, protective garments, automotive, home appliances, and wind energy. Its materials are used in applications such as acoustic fabrics for automotive noise control, emergency escape chute components, therapeutic bedding, medical fabrics, protective apparel, and window treatment fabrics. The company maintains long-standing customer relationships through collaborative R&D and a focus on product quality.

Precision Fabrics was the first ISO-qualified textile supplier in the United States, achieving ISO 9001 registration in 1993 and updating to ISO 9001:2015 in 2018. The company says its differentiation lies in the breadth of its technical capabilities, the depth of its team's expertise, and a commitment to innovation that drives problem-solving across diverse markets.

A chemical engineer by training, Chow moved from Pennsylvania after a career at Allied Corporation to start the company, initially focusing on plastic injection molding, composites, and CNC machining with an emphasis on lean and agile processes.

The company provides end-to-end manufacturing services including plastic injection molding, metal injection molding (MIM), silicone molding, CNC milling and turning, CNC electrical discharge machining (EDM), 6-axis robotic assembly and composite casting, sub-assembly, reverse engineering, 3D printing, and RFID tagging. It handles projects from rapid prototyping through short- and long-run production, operating as a one-stop shop that integrates design, mold optimization, and production under one roof.

Prime serves commercial, industrial, and military customers across agriculture, automotive, construction, defense, technology, healthcare, and telecommunications sectors. Its client roster includes Fortune 500 organizations such as Northrop Grumman, Agilent Technologies, Ciena, Snap-On Power Tools, and the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory, alongside government agencies.

The company differentiates itself through a blend of manual craftsmanship with robotics and automation, a lean-and-agile manufacturing philosophy, and a commitment to reducing the need for multiple suppliers by covering design through final assembly.

The company emphasizes a hybrid model: the focus and expertise of a small company paired with the resources and purchasing power of a large corporation. about:
Progressive Plastics, Inc. operates from Clover, South Carolina, a location centrally positioned between Charlotte, North Carolina, and Greenville, South Carolina with easy access to major highways and an international airport. The company was founded in 1986 by Keith Brackett, who identified a market need for a short-run molder capable of processing small quantities for both individuals and businesses. That focus later expanded to include insert molding, a process Brackett recognized as too labor-intensive for larger molders.

Today, Progressive Plastics functions as a small custom injection molder of thermoplastic products. Its core capability is plastic injection molding, including insert molding that encapsulates metal or other non-plastic inserts in a single operation. The company also provides development design and consultation services to guide customers through the product creation process. Its product line centers on agricultural packaging, notably a range of fruit baskets — round half-gallon, half-bushel, peck, and rectangular half-gallon containers — designed to protect produce such as peaches, berries, apples, and tomatoes from field to packing shed.

The primary market served is agriculture, where growers, distributors, and packers rely on the company's durable thermoplastic containers. Because the operation is geared toward short runs, it also accommodates individual entrepreneurs and small businesses needing limited quantities. The company states its goal is total customer satisfaction through defect-free processes and continuous improvement, with the owner directly accessible for questions and order assistance.

Brackett started the business after seeing that larger molders avoided short-run and labor-intensive insert molding work. That founding principle remains: the firm positions itself on personable, knowledgeable service, on-time delivery, and a willingness to handle orders that larger competitors decline.

about:
Propper Manufacturing Company, Inc. operates from Long Island City, New York. Founded in 1945, the family-owned business has remained under family stewardship for nearly eight decades. The company was established to address sterilization monitoring needs in healthcare settings.

The company manufactures disposable medical devices with a focus on sterilization monitoring. Its product line includes chemical indicators (Type 1 and Type 5), biological indicators (Duo-Spore®), Bowie-Dick test packs, EO sterilization monitoring tools (including the FDA-cleared EO Chex™ indicator tape), and reusable process challenge devices (Vapor Line® Helix-Type PCD). They also produce Magnalume™ disposable laryngoscope blades made from high-strength polycarbonate, microscope slides, cover glass, hemacytometers, surgical blades, and other laboratory and surgical instruments. The facility offers private labeling and OEM manufacturing services, and runs a Culture Service Program for biological monitoring.

Propper serves hospitals, laboratories, veterinary clinics, dental offices, biotech and pharmaceutical companies, scientific research institutions, and body modification professionals. The company also supports international markets and provides OEM solutions for major healthcare brands.

The company states its mission is to provide high-quality infection control products that aid in eliminating hospital-acquired infections. It emphasizes investment in groundbreaking products and customer education through platforms like Propper Connects.

Quality Bus & Truck Parts operates from Big Lake, Minnesota, and was founded in 2018. The business grew out of a recognition that school districts, fleet operators, and mechanics needed a dependable source for older, hard‑to‑find, and obsolete bus and truck components. After years of selling new parts through its sister company, Midwest Bus Parts, the founders identified a gap in the market for cost‑effective, high‑quality recycled parts and launched this venture to fill it.

The company specializes in sourcing, salvaging, and refurbishing used and remanufactured parts for school buses and medium‑duty trucks. Its inventory spans thousands of items across categories such as engine components, electrical systems, drivetrain assemblies, braking, HVAC, and body parts. Operations include nationwide distribution with international shipping capabilities, a parts lookup service, and a physical facility that also provides expert maintenance, inspections, and service work. Additionally, the firm runs a vehicle recycling program and purchases used school buses and medium‑duty trucks for teardown.

Customers range from individual bus owners to large municipal fleets. The company explicitly serves school districts, transportation contractors, fleet maintenance facilities, municipal fleets, commercial businesses, independent repair shops, bus owners and builders, and individual customers. Supported brands include Blue Bird, IC Bus, Thomas Built Buses, International, GMC, Freightliner, and Ford, with common engine platforms such as International DT466, MaxxForce series, Cummins 5.9 and ISB6.7, CAT C7 and 3126, Mercedes MBE series, Detroit Diesel, Ford Power Stroke, and Chevy Duramax.

Quality Bus & Truck Parts positions itself as more than a salvage yard, emphasizing reliable solutions over simple used‑part sales. Its stated differentiators are a deep inventory of hard‑to‑find components, cost‑effective remanufactured alternatives, industry‑specific expertise, and fast shipping. The mission is framed as "Honoring God by serving and growing our team, customers and suppliers," backed by core values that include a can‑do attitude, problem solving, sacrifice for others, honesty, and continuous growth.

In‑house R&D develops proprietary dough flavors and fillings, and the company uses RedZone manufacturing software for real‑time production monitoring.

old_description: designs and manufactures electrical automation control components. We provide standard products that have many applications with a variety of customers and custom products. The custom products are typically designed for use in our customer's equipment and machinery control systems.
about:
R-K Electronics is based in Mason, Ohio, and traces its roots to February 1949 when Bill Keller and John Runge founded R-K Electric Company, Inc. as a panel builder serving steel mills, machine tool builders, and paper manufacturers across Ohio, Indiana, and Kentucky.

Today the company designs and manufactures a range of electronic automation control components, from intrinsically safe low‑voltage relays to 600‑volt three‑phase monitoring controls. In addition to its standard product line, R-K develops custom processor‑based embedded controllers—dedicated PLCs with hardware, firmware, and packaging tailored to OEM specifications—for equipment and machinery control systems.

R-K’s customers span the electrical controls industry and OEMs in sectors such as heating and refrigeration, pumping and level control, as well as the original steel, machine tool, and paper markets. The company supplies both off‑the‑shelf components and fully customized control solutions built to each OEM’s operating requirements.

The founder’s original decision to start the business because they “couldn’t do any worse working for themselves” evolved into a stated philosophy of customer‑driven innovation: R-K emphasizes listening to customers to create control components with unique features that simplify control requirements and make customers more successful. Ongoing development includes controls that interface with the company’s own color touch screens.

old_description: From statement pieces to one-of-a-kind builds, we specialize in custom fabrication that brings your ideas to life.
about:
R&D Fabworks, LLC is based in Crittenden, Kentucky, and was founded in 2016 by Garrett Daniels. After studying mechanical engineering at the University of Kentucky and earning AWS certifications at the Knight School of Welding, Daniels spent years in production welding and machining while building the business on nights and weekends. He committed to the company full-time in 2019 with the support of his wife, Amanda, and the shop has since grown from a custom off-road fabrication startup into a full-service metal fabrication and welding operation serving the Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky region.

The company provides custom metal fabrication, welding (MIG, TIG, stick), CNC plasma cutting, plate and sheet rolling, tube rolling and bending, and structural fabrication including mezzanines, catwalks, safety railings, ADA ramps and handrails. It also offers marine construction and repair such as marina builds, boat lifts, and aluminum boat repair, as well as mobile welding for on-site equipment and trailer repair. The shop handles one-off prototypes through large production runs and works with materials ranging from carbon steel and stainless steel to titanium, Inconel, Monel, Hastelloy, copper-nickel alloys, and copper and brass brazing.

R&D Fabworks serves residential homeowners, commercial property owners, contractors, industrial facilities, marinas, and fleet operators primarily within a three-hour radius of Cincinnati. Typical projects include custom staircases, railings, and outdoor structures for homes; safety railings, ADA-compliant access systems, and structural platforms for commercial and industrial buildings; and emergency mobile welding for heavy equipment, trailers, and cast-iron components.

The company emphasizes a ‘do it right, don’t cut corners’ philosophy, stating that it treats every project as the only one on the schedule and backs its work with over 47 AWS certifications, licensed and insured status, and a commitment to fast response times for emergency repairs.

about:
RDI Foods, LLC is a food consulting firm based in Raleigh, North Carolina. Founded in June 2002 by Dr. Richard "Rody" Hawkins after 17 years at ConAgra Foods and Philip Morris (Kraft Foods), the company was created as a resource to help food companies solve problems, create value, and improve margins. The principals—Dr. Hawkins, Larry Chandler (food process and project management), Steve Klawiter (packaging systems), and Dr. Sarid Shefet (innovative food processing)—collectively hold over 85 years of industry experience and 28 patents.

The firm specializes in food product research, development, and plant implementation. It designs and coordinates innovative solutions for established food companies, including new product and process development for domestic and international markets, cross-functional team leadership for production launches, raw material cost reduction, process efficiency improvements, and shelf-life evaluation. RDI Foods also develops and implements Safe Quality Food (SQF) programs, and has expertise in military product development and specification writing under a Cooperative Research and Development Agreement (CRADA) with the U.S. Army Soldier Systems Command in Natick, Massachusetts.

Clients span the food industry, from commercial manufacturers of shelf-stable and preserved foods to the U.S. military. The company has worked with the U.S. Army since 1993 on shelf-stable sandwiches, earning an Excellence in Research Award. It also partners with food companies on joint ventures, sharing profits from co-developed products. Examples include pepperoni and pizza production consulting, and projects for five food companies in a 12-month period.

RDI Foods distinguishes itself through its principals' deep technical expertise in shelf-stable foods, processing, and packaging, combined with a consulting model that moves beyond advice to hands-on implementation in production environments. The firm's SQF programs have been recognized as industry models, and its military R&D track record demonstrates capability in high-stakes, regulated product development.

The company began by refurbishing furniture for large corporations and reselling high-quality used systems to smaller organizations across the Mid-Atlantic region, including Aberdeen, Baltimore, Columbia, and Washington, DC.

Today Re-form operates a 50,000-square-foot warehouse and production facility in Baltimore where nearly 50 skilled upholsterers, painters, woodworkers, warehouse technicians, installers, designers, and project managers handle warehousing, inventory management, furniture delivery and installation, office decommissioning, space planning, and furniture refurbishment. The facility supports remanufacturing of Herman Miller, Haworth, and Steelcase systems furniture, along with paint refinishing, seating reupholstery, and laminate fabrication. An online inventory portal gives clients remote access to stored assets and allows them to request delivery or installation.

The company serves enterprise-sized corporations, government agencies, and other organizations undergoing relocation, renovation, consolidation, or new-space openings throughout the Mid-Atlantic. It also taps a national installation network for out-of-state projects. Clients rely on Re-form for coordinated workplace transitions that encompass asset tracking, responsible reuse and recycling, and phased deployment.

Re-form positions itself as a single-source partner for workplace logistics, emphasizing practical, flexible solutions that reduce waste, control costs, and extend the useful life of existing furniture. Its combined services—warehousing, asset management, installation, decommissioning, and design—are intended to keep organizations organized and adaptable as workplace needs change.

name: Reclaiming Iowa
old_description: Reclaiming Iowa specializes in custom commercial and residential heirloom furniture and decor made from locally sourced reclaimed timbers and hardwoods.
about:
Reclaiming Iowa operates from West Des Moines, Iowa, where it was founded in 2008 by Kevin Dubay. Dubay holds a Bachelor of Fine Arts from the Kansas City Art Institute and a Master's in Furniture Design and Manufacturing from the University of Arizona, and he launched the studio to combine artistic vision with hands-on craftsmanship.

The company builds custom commercial and residential heirloom furniture and architectural woodwork using locally sourced reclaimed timbers and live‑edge hardwood slabs. Every piece is made to order — about 90 percent of projects are fully custom — and the workshop handles everything from consultation and design through handcrafting, kiln‑drying slabs to 6 percent moisture content, and finishing with a durable hard wax oil. Restoration services are not offered.

Clients span residential homeowners and a range of commercial sectors: restaurants and bars (dining tables, bar tops, back bars, feature walls), retail (countertops, shelving, product displays), and office or flex spaces (conference tables, desks, reception pieces). The studio has completed projects for businesses across Iowa, delivering and installing each piece statewide at no extra charge.

Dubay started Reclaiming Iowa to provide furniture that fits a client's exact space and style while preserving the history of salvaged wood. When possible, pieces are labeled with the original building name, location, and construction date, turning each item into a conversation piece and an environmentally sustainable choice.

old_description: Our philosophy is and always has been simple. We succeed when our customers succeed.
about:
Red Fox Innovations was founded in 2015 in Blaine, Minnesota, as a domestic response to the offshoring of cut-and-sew work. The company began with a focus on providing reliable, cost-competitive manufacturing without sacrificing quality, and has since grown into a full-service contract manufacturer.

Today the firm operates an FDA-registered, ISO 13485-certified facility where over 160 employees produce more than one million units annually across 1,000-plus unique product designs. All work is performed on-site using automated fabric cutters, programmable sewing machines, large-format RF welding equipment, and laser cutting systems. Services span industrial sewing, die and laser cutting, RF/ultrasonic/hot-air welding, material sourcing, and full product design and development from prototype to volume production.

The customer base ranges from large public corporations to start-ups, with core markets in medical devices, outdoor and specialty retail, and military/government contracts requiring Berry Amendment compliance. The company also supports direct-to-consumer brands seeking U.S.-made soft goods.

Red Fox merged with major client Caerus Corp in 2022 to combine resources under brands such as Animal Ortho Care and OrthoCor Medical. The founding philosophy — “we succeed when our customers succeed” — remains central, reinforced by proprietary factory-management software that tracks real-time productivity and quality metrics at every workstation.

about:
Red Oak Fabrication operates from Red Oak, Iowa, where it was established in 1913 as the Pike Machine Shop. Renamed Red Oak Machine Co. in 1923, the business was purchased by Ted Fort in stages between 1944 and 1946 and has remained in the Fort family for four generations. Today the company runs four facilities in southwest Iowa, with Jeff Fort and his three sons — Jacob, Jordan, and Justin — serving as owners and managers.

The shop provides a full range of metal fabrication services: plasma cutting on two Alltra tables (up to 3-inch capacity), fiber laser cutting with three Bystronic and Cutlite systems (including the first Cutlite Penta 20 kW in the U.S. with fully automated load/unload), tube laser cutting, CNC milling and turning across 11 machining centers, press brake forming up to 350 tons, robotic and manual welding (11 AWS D1.1‑certified welders), steel blasting, and powder coating. The powder coating line uses the only GFS booths in Iowa that combine blasting with a three‑stage wash, and is certified to AAMA 2603, 2604, and 2605.

Red Oak Fabrication serves industrial and commercial customers requiring precision metal parts, welded assemblies, and finished coatings.

The company emphasizes its multi‑generational family ownership, direct owner involvement in daily operations, and unique powder‑coating capabilities — particularly the combined blast‑and‑wash booth and 60‑color in‑house palette with custom matching in 10 business days. Turnaround for coating is typically 7–10 days, with 24‑hour expedited service available.

about:
Reed Food Technology was established in 1995 as a family-owned and operated custom food product developer and private label manufacturer in Pearl, Mississippi. The company's foundation is built on a passion for food and family, a philosophy that extends through every team member. A sister facility, operating under the name Tastemaker Foods, is located in Hernando, Mississippi, giving the business two manufacturing sites in the state.

The company specializes in custom food manufacturing and private label sauce production, guiding clients through a four-step process: discovery and formula development in a state-of-the-art lab and test kitchen, testing and approval, scale-up and packaging (including retail label design, portion pouches, totes, and bags), and ongoing quality support. Both facilities are SQF Level 3 certified, and the company maintains memberships in the Research Chefs Association and the Institute of Food Technologists. They emphasize flexibility, offering low minimum order quantities and quick turnaround on lab testing and sample requests.

Its customer base includes over 300 clients and more than 2,000 developed products, ranging from startups to established brands looking for recipe improvement or new product design.

The company says its differentiation lies in its family-driven culture, scientific approach to food innovation, and commitment to integrity—delivering high-quality, cost-effective products with some of the lowest minimums in the industry.

Regal Plastic Supply Company, a family-owned business established in 1954, operates from Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. The company began as a supplier of see-through and industrial plastics and has grown to serve the Midwest through 15 locations.

These capabilities support needs from single-piece prototypes to high-volume production runs.

Regal Plastic serves industrial, commercial, and custom fabrication customers across sectors such as signage, printing, exhibits, manufacturing, agriculture, and construction. Its materials and fabrication services are used for protective barriers, windows, displays, gears, bushings, bearings, packaging, and other applications requiring chemical resistance, impact strength, or optical clarity.

The company attributes its success to an experienced leadership team, a commitment to research and innovation, quick delivery, and a one-stop-shop model that combines material supply with on-site fabrication.

The company provides a broad portfolio spanning analog and mixed-signal circuits, power management devices, embedded processing (MCUs and MPUs), and connectivity products. Its technology includes GaN power devices, GreenPAK programmable mixed-signal ICs, and high-performance computing solutions. Renesas employs over 21,000 professionals across more than 30 countries, with design, sales, and support operations worldwide.

Customers include automotive OEMs and tier-1 suppliers, industrial automation vendors, data-center and robotics developers, and IoT device makers. The firm's solutions appear in applications such as electric-vehicle power trains, factory automation, AI data-center power delivery, and low-power edge-computing endpoints.

Renesas emphasizes its system-level expertise and the industry's widest product portfolio as differentiators, aiming to reduce development effort through reusable design assets and pin-compatible device families. Its stated purpose, 'To Make Our Lives Easier,' underscores a focus on power-efficient, sustainable semiconductor solutions.
